manager_rule: When compiler_kelvin_omission fires (Rule 33) AND total-stub-absorption is active (absorbed + trimmed_spurs + removed_orphans >= n_stubs, per Rule 34) AND M_actual EQUALS 1 (exactly one cable index present in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines') AND that same cable index appeared in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines' in at least one of the two immediately preceding rounds: execute a routing-layer occupancy query on a 6mm bounding box centred on the failing cable's shunt pads, using the identical procedure specified in Rule 35 — report per copper layer: (i) via count within the bounding box, (ii) track-segment count, (iii) net names of any segments or vias belonging to nets other than /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO for the failing cable N. Log 'kelvin_congestion_diagnostic_m1' with fields: (a) round number, (b) failing cable index, (c) per-layer via counts, (d) per-layer track-segment counts, (e) list of foreign net names present. If any copper layer within the bounding box carries more than 8 vias OR more than 12 track segments belonging to nets other than /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO, classify that cable as congestion_blocked and: (1) add a narrow rectangular routing-exclusion keepout (minimum 0.5mm wide, covering the shunt inner-edge escape path, excluding all nets except /SENSEC{N}_HI and /SENSEC{N}_LO) to the FR input for the next round before force-injected stub injection; (2) log 'kelvin_congestion_keepout_added_m1' with the keepout geometry and cable index; (3) ensure the force-injected Kelvin stubs from Rule 33 target pad coordinates within the reserved channel. If the occupancy query is not executable (board state unavailable), log 'kelvin_congestion_diagnostic_m1_failed' and escalate immediately without FR dispatch. This rule is additive to Rules 33 and 34 and does not replace or defer any action those rules independently mandate; it closes the M_actual=1 diagnostic gap left by Rule 35's M_actual>=2 requirement.
